forecaster_note: Easing south swell and some short-period NE wind wave are giving peaky, fun-sized surf — chest to head at S exposures, around chest high elsewhere. Cleanest in the morning with light NW winds, then NE picks up again mid-morning, so look to more sheltered S-facing spots. — Surfline forecaster Hugh McDowell (Thu 1 Oct)

wind.summary: Light NNW 9 kph — offshore at dawn and through 9am (gusts ~20). NE onshore from noon, 24 kph (gusts 30) by 3pm.

days.label: Today
days.note: Peaky NE wind swell (4.9ft @ 7s, 208 kJ — fun, not powerful) with a fading 2ft S swell, on a light NNW offshore dawn. Dee Why gets the NE at its best angle; Long Reef picks up the most size. Best 6:30–10am — then the NE turns onshore from noon. High tide 11:03am. Surfline sizes are conservative; the forecaster calls chest high, more at S exposures.

swells.label: Dominant short-period NE wind swell — the good angle
Secondary S swell (dead-S angle, wraps poorly at Dee Why)

dee-why.window: Light NNW offshore till ~9am, cross-shore by noon, NE onshore from 3pm. NE 48° is the ideal angle here — peaky beachbreak, go early before the NE lumps it up. The dead-S 178° component wraps badly, so favour peaks with NE in them.

tip.label: NE peaks — frontside at the Point
tip.text: Short-period NE is the good angle at Dee Why. Frontside rights at the Point, backside lefts on the beach peaks. Only 7s, so it's punchy rather than powerful — commit to the takeoff and stay on the drive.

swells.label: Dominant short-period NE wind swell — the good angle
Secondary S swell (dead-S angle, wraps poorly at Dee Why)

long-reef.window: Picks up the most size of the four. Light offshore till ~9am, cross-shore NE from noon. Reef handles the little S swell better than the beachies.

tip.label: Frontside rights off the reef
tip.text: Waist to shoulder with some S in the mix. Pick the sections that line up — 7s wind swell can back off between sets, so be patient and position on the peak.

swells.label: Dominant short-period NE wind swell — the good angle
Secondary S swell (dead-S angle, wraps poorly at Dee Why)

curl-curl.window: Light offshore early, then NE cross-shore. Fun and peaky; find the bank with the best shape.

tip.label: Find the bank
tip.text: Smaller and peaky — look for the peak holding its shape and take the shoulder. Good for a flowy session.

swells.label: Dominant short-period NE wind swell — the good angle

manly.window: Cross-shore NNW at dawn, onshore NE from noon. Smallest of the four but the most sheltered later in the day.

tip.label: Sheltered fallback
tip.text: Smaller and softer. Only worth it if you want an easy one or the NE has wrecked the others.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Peaky NE eases to waist–chest. NW winds cleanest through the morning; NE likely returns later, best at the sheltered N corners — though winds could go offshore again late. Sizes estimated from the forecaster text.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Sat is the pick: winds should swing favourable and clean up an easing NE wind swell, maybe a little local S swell — fun peaky surf, some clean options. Sun turns S 20 kph+ from dawn, so get Sat. Forecaster says it's still uncertain and will shift — recheck Friday. Daylight saving starts Sun 4 Oct (clocks forward 2am): sunrise ~6:29am AEDT.
